Mechanistic genome-environment association tests.

mechGEA.Rd

Core functions for the mechanistic GEA-with-migration pipeline, producing output files and plots in the working directory (and returned as an object). For large data (e.g. many SNPs), consider running this on small Phred batches and then combining.

Usage

mechGEA(
  Phred,
  patch_info,
  patches_xy,
  env,
  migration_results = NULL,
  N_sim_mig = 100,
  migration_loci = 1000,
  k_sd = 4,
  p0 = 20,
  seed = 42,
  migration_model = "migration_fast",
  max_attempts_mig = 10,
  target_div_pct_mig = 1,
  target_rhat_pct_mig = 1,
  chains_mig = 4,
  iter_sampling_mig = 1000,
  iter_warmup_mig = 1000,
  max_treedepth_mig = 12,
  refresh_mig = 200,
  mig_plot_threshold = 0.4,
  mig_plot_topn = 2,
  mig_plot_binsize = 1,
  chains_gea = 2,
  refresh_gea = 200,
  iter_warmup_gea = 250,
  iter_sampling_gea = 500,
  CI = 0.95,
  env_colors = NULL,
  stop_after_migration = FALSE,
  par = parallel::detectCores() - 2
)

prepare_mig_data(
  Phred,
  patch_info,
  patches_xy,
  env,
  migration_loci,
  N_sim_mig,
  seed = 42
)

estimate_migration(
  migration_data,
  migration_model = "migration_fast",
  max_attempts_mig = 10,
  target_div_pct_mig = 1,
  target_rhat_pct_mig = 1,
  chains_mig = 4,
  iter_sampling_mig = 1000,
  iter_warmup_mig = 1000,
  max_treedepth_mig = 12,
  refresh_mig = 200,
  par = parallel::detectCores() - 2
)

run_stan_GEA_model(
  stan_data,
  migration_results,
  k_sd = 4,
  p0 = 20,
  refresh_gea = 100,
  chains_gea = 2,
  iter_warmup_gea = 250,
  iter_sampling_gea = 500,
  seed = 42,
  par = parallel::detectCores() - 2
)

estimate_neff(stan_data)

beta_summary(beta_draw, nloci, nenv)

plot_migration(
  migration_results,
  migration_data,
  patches_xy,
  mig_plot_threshold = 0.4,
  mig_plot_topn = 2,
  mig_plot_binsize = 1
)

plot_gea(
  stan_data,
  migration_results,
  beta_draw,
  beta_summary,
  rho_kappa_mu,
  env_names,
  CI = 0.95,
  env_colors = NULL
)

Arguments

Phred

Phred-scaled genotype liklelihoods, as generated from a .beagle or .beagle.gz file by beagle2pl. See example_gl$likelihoods for an example.

patch_info

data.frame or similar. Patch information for each sample in a two-column data.frame with column names ind_id and patch. Important note: samples MUST be sorted in blocks by patch (all samples in one patch must be in blocks). Data fitting this format can be produced by prepare_metadata.

patches_xy

data.frame or similar. Spatial coordinates for each patch, with three columns named patch, lat, and lon. Must be ordered identically to order of patch appearance in patch_info. Data fitting this format can be produced by prepare_metadata.

env

data.frame or similar. Uncorrelated, scaled environmental variables for each patch, with N + 1 columns. The first column must be named patch and contain patch names. The additional N columns can have any name and can contain Z-scaled env data (mean = 0, sd = 1). Patches must be ordered identically to order of patch appearance in patch_info. Data fitting this format can be produced by prepare_metadata and uncorrelated envs can be selected using prune_envs.

migration_results

list or NULL, default NULL. If provided, mechGEA will use migration results in the list format produced by estimate_migration rather than re-running with the provided data. This is useful if you wish to assess migration once with a set of loci and then use that assessment for other genomic chunks (see stop_after_migration to estimate migration and then stop the model).

N_sim_mig

integer, default 100. Number of times genotypes are re-sampled when estimating the diversity for migration. Ignored if migration_results are provided.

migration_loci

integer, default 1000. Number of loci to use from Phred to use for estimating migration. Must be equal to or less than the total number of provided loci. Ignored if migration_results are provided; if less than 1000, will be set to 1000 or the number of loci in the dataset.

k_sd

numeric, default 4. NIKUNJ HERE PLEASE!

p0

numeric, default 20. NIKUNJ HERE PLEASE!

seed

integer, default 42. Seed used for all model steps.

migration_model

character, default "migration_fast". Choice of model for estimating migration. Options are "migration_fast" or "migration_M3b". See details. NIKUNJ HERE PLEASE!

max_attempts_mig

integer, default 10. Number of times to try fitting the migration model. If the model does not converge after max_attempts_mig tries, the best fit model will be used.

target_div_pct_mig

numeric, default 1. Maximum percentage of divergences allowed during migration model fitting.

target_rhat_pct_mig

numeric, default 1. Maximum percentage of rhat > 1.05 allowed during fitting.

chains_mig

integer, default 4. Number of chains to run for the Bayesian migration model fitting.

iter_sampling_mig

integer, default 1000. Number of sampling iterations to run the Bayesian migration model fitting.

iter_warmup_mig

integer, default 1000. Number of warm-up/burn-in iterations to run the Bayesian migration model fitting.

max_treedepth_mig

integer, default 12. Maximum tree-depth to use during Bayesian migration model fitting.

refresh_mig

integer, default 200. Controls how often model progress is reported during Bayesian migration model fitting.

mig_plot_threshold

numeric, default 0.4. For plotting migration model results, controls the migration strength threshold above which migration connections will be included in networks.

mig_plot_topn

integer, default 2. Number of migratory connections to consider for each pixel when plotting migration networks. NIKUNJ HERE PLEASE!

mig_plot_binsize

integer, default 1. NIKUNJ HERE PLEASE!

chains_gea

integer, default 2. Number of chains to run for the GEA model.

refresh_gea

integer, default 200. Controls how often model progress is reported during GEA model fitting.

iter_warmup_gea

integer, default 200. Number of warm-up/burn-in iterations to run the during GEA model fitting.

iter_sampling_gea

integer, default 250. Number of sampling iterations to run the during GEA model fitting.

CI

numeric, default 0.95. Confidence interval to plot for the GEA model.

env_colors

character or NULL, default NULL. Vector of colors for environmental variables.

stop_after_migration

logical, default FALSE. If TRUE, stop the model after running estimate_migration. This is useful if you wish to assess migration once with a set of loci and then use that assessment for other genomic chunks (see migration_results to pick up the model with the results in other chunks.).

par

integer, default parallel::detectCores() - 2, two less than the available cores. Maximum number of cores to allocate for model fitting; the number of cores per chain will be par/N_chains.

migration_data

list containing data for migration model, in the format produced by prepare_mig_data$migration_data.

stan_data

list containing data for the stan GEA model fitting, in the format produced by prepare_mig_data$stan_data.

beta_draw

beta parameter sampling/draw data from a fit GEA model, as produced by run_stan_GEA_model$beta_draw.

nloci

integer, number of loci in the source data for the stan model.

nenv

integer, number of environmental variables in the source data for the stan model.

beta_summary

beta parameter summary data from a fit GEA model, as produced by beta_summary$beta_summary.

rho_kappa_mu

parameter fit data from a GEA model, as produced by run_stan_GEA_model$rho_kapp_mu.

env_names

character, vector of environmental variable names.

Value

A nested list containing model outputs. Different modules may return different portions of the following list; mechGEA will return every part. NIKUNJ, DETAIL WOULD BE GREAT!

  • SNP_pvalues: A data.table containing associations (nlogp, \(-\log_{e}\) transformed p-values) for each SNP (numbered 1:n by input order Phred) compared to each environmental variable.

  • GEA_results: A list containing summaries of the GEA model fits.

  • migration_results: A n by n matrix where n is the number of patches; estimated migration rates between each patch.

  • Neff_results: A list containing the effective sample size estimates for each locus vs each environmental variable.

  • migration_plot: Plots of isolation-by-distance and migration rates between patches.

  • GEA_plots: Manhattan plot, model fit visualization, and migration-selection balances for each significant correlation from the GEA.

  • stan_and_migration_data: Formatted data which was used by the GEA and migration models.

Functions

  • mechGEA(): The full mechanistic GEA model pipeline.

  • prepare_mig_data(): Prepare migration data (and stan) data for modeling. Consider running with mechGEA for the full pipeline.

  • estimate_migration(): Run the migration estimation model. Consider running with mechGEA for the full pipeline.

  • run_stan_GEA_model(): Run the Bayesian mechanistic GEA model. Consider running with mechGEA for the full pipeline.

  • estimate_neff(): Estimate effective sample sizes for data for run_stan_GEA_model. Consider running with mechGEA for the full pipeline.

  • beta_summary(): Calculate parameter summaries from a run_stan_GEA_model. Consider running with mechGEA for the full pipeline.

  • plot_migration(): Plot migration model results. Consider running with mechGEA for the full pipeline.

  • plot_gea(): Plot GEA model results. Consider running with mechGEA for the full pipeline.

References

Goel, N., et al. (2026). Identifying adaptive variation in spatially structured populations using low-coverage whole-genome sequencing data. Molecular Biology and Evolution, 43(10), msag255. https://doi.org/10.1093/molbev/msag255

William Hemstrom, Nikunj Goel

Examples

# a basic run of the full pipeline
## example beagle file:
beagle <- system.file("extdata", "example.beagle.gz", package = "mechGEA")
## convert the formats of the data and metadata
phred <- beagle2pl(beagle, lines = 1:150)
input_data <- prepare_metadata(sample_metadata)
## run the pipeline
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
res <- mechGEA(phred,
               patch_info = input_data$patch_info,
               patches_xy = input_data$patches_xy,
               migration_loci = 50,
               env = input_data$env,
               iter_sampling_gea = 100,
               iter_warmup_gea = 200,
               iter_sampling_mig = 100,
               iter_warmup_mig = 200)
} # }

# Run only up until the migration calculation and plot results
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
res_mig <- mechGEA(phred,
                   patch_info = input_data$patch_info,
                   patches_xy = input_data$patches_xy,
                   migration_loci = 50,
                   env = input_data$env,
                   iter_sampling_mig = 100,
                   iter_warmup_mig = 200,
                   stop_after_migration = TRUE)
p <- plot_migration(migration_results = res_mig$migration_results,
       migration_data = res_mig$stan_and_migration_data$migration_data,
       patches_xy = input_data$patches_xy,
       mig_plot_threshold = 0.4,
       mig_plot_topn = 2,
       mig_plot_binsize = 1)
} # }

# using a pre-computed migration result (great if running a migration once
# and applying across many chunks)
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
res_ <- mechGEA(phred,
               patch_info = input_data$patch_info,
               patches_xy = input_data$patches_xy,
               migration_loci = 50,
               env = input_data$env,
               iter_sampling_gea = 100,
               iter_warmup_gea = 200,
               migration_results = res_mig$migration_results)
} # }
